newsitem.title: ITALY: Employers want confrontation - Italy metal unions.
newsitem.headline: Employers want confrontation - Italy metal unions.

text.p: Italian metalworkers' unions, which have staged a series of strikes in a bitter pay dispute, accused employers group Federmeccanica on Tuesday of provocation after it again rejected a government arbitration proposal.
"Federmeccanica has reopened a phase of confrontation," said Claudio Sabatini, secretary general of the FIOM union.
"If it does not clarify its proposals in precise terms, it is difficult to see how we can arrive at real negotiations."
Federmeccanica earlier reaffirmed it would not accept a government proposal to end the months-long row.

"At this moment there are no negotiations and I do not know when they will be unblocked," director-general Michele Figurati said after a meeting. "We won't deal on the basis of (the government suggestion. The cost has to be lower."
Domenico Fresilli, national secretary of the UGL union, said he had been hoping for some "minimal opening up to dialogue" on the part of the employers.

"All this smacks strongly of provocation to us," he said. The situation has been stalled since June when the last contract expired. Metalworkers have staged two eight-hour strikes and last week began another phase of stoppages to press their demands.
The dispute centres on the interpretation of a landmark 1993 wage deal, which scrapped automatic index-linked wage rises.

The government has suggested that management offer workers a monthly pay rise of 200,000 lire per month for the 1996-98 contract to compensate for inflation and unions accepted that, even though it was below their 230,000 lire demand.
Federmeccanica is refusing to pay more than 139,000 lire per month and says the government suggestion is inflationary.
But Luigi Angeletti of the UILM union said Federmeccanica's reference in a statement after its meeting to "legitimate salary expectations of workers" offered some hope.
"If they are sincere...then we've made a step forward," he said.
